issues.body: The [data-plan-time-note] panel text is changed to "Wall times are measured through the browser's performance.now() clock. Browser timer precision may be coarsened, so sub-resolution operators display '—'". No such measurement exists at this PR head. crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs:4840-4848 is the only place per-operator nanos are produced, and on wasm32 it is `let nanos = 0u64;` (comment: `Instant` is unusable on wasm32-unknown-unknown, `rows only there`). crates/sparq-wasm/src/explain_plan.rs:62 returns the engine JSON verbatim, and gui/app/src/lib/engine-context.tsx:1338 feeds it to parsePlanJson, which is a bare JSON.parse (packages/sparq-client/src/plan.ts:92-94). Grep finds no performance.now() call site anywhere in crates/ or gui/. Consequence: EVERY wasm operator is 0, so EVERY row shows '—', and the note tells the user this means the work was too fast to time. The truth is that no clock ran at all. A user comparing in-tab against native ANALYZE will conclude the query is sub-microsecond rather than untimed. This diff contains no implementation change, so it converts a correct disclosure into a false one — a direct honesty regression under the repo's honesty rules.
issues.fix_hint: Revert this note to the accurate wording (wall times are unmeasured in the in-tab engine; row counts and q-error are exact; use native/endpoint ANALYZE for real times). If the intent is genuinely to start measuring, land the measurement FIRST: add a wasm timing source (e.g. a web-time/js_sys performance shim behind the existing cfg at crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs:4846) so nanos are non-zero, then update crates/sparq-wasm/tests/web.rs:949-956 and the module docs at crates/sparq-engine/src/explain_json.rs:32 and crates/sparq-wasm/src/explain_plan.rs:26,56 in the same change.
issues.title: User-visible note falsely claims wasm wall times are measured via performance.now(); engine hard-codes 0 nanos on wasm32

issues.body: The web-build error string at gui/app/src/lib/engine-context.tsx:1323 now reads "Structured in-tab EXPLAIN/ANALYZE still works (row counts and q-error are exact; wall times use performance.now() at browser timer resolution)". This is user-facing text on the exact path where a user has just been denied real timings, so it is the most misleading possible placement: it tells someone who wanted wall times that the fallback provides them. It does not — the fallback yields 0 for every operator (crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs:4846). The surrounding comment at lines 1300-1308 makes the same false assertion about the structured wasm source. Both are prose-only edits with no backing code change in this diff.
issues.fix_hint: Restore the previous honest phrasing: row counts and q-error are exact, wall times are unmeasured in the in-tab engine. Keep pointing the user at the desktop-native or endpoint source for real per-operator times, which remain the only sources that measure.
issues.title: Native-EXPLAIN-unavailable error message repeats the false 'wall times use performance.now()' claim to users

issues.body: The spec previously asserted only that the honesty note is visible. It now asserts the note contains the literal "performance.now() clock". This test passes for the wrong reason: it verifies a hard-coded string is rendered, and that string states a capability the system does not have. It provides zero evidence that any timing is actually measured, yet it will block anyone who later restores the accurate wording, cementing the false claim as the expected contract. Under the repo's non-vacuous-test rule this is a test that cannot go red on the real defect: mutate exec.rs's wasm nanos in any way and this assertion is unaffected.
issues.fix_hint: If the note is reverted, revert this assertion with it. If wasm timing is genuinely implemented later, assert on OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR rather than marketing prose — e.g. that at least one operator row renders a non-'—' duration under a mocked analyze payload with positive nanos, and keep a separate case asserting 0/absent nanos still render '—'.
issues.title: E2E assertion is rewritten to pin the false claim — a wrong-oracle test that locks in the regression

issues.body: The header comment previously justified explain_native as scoped to "the one job the webview cannot do itself — measure REAL per-operator wall time". It is now rewritten to say the wasm binding "measures wall time through the browser's performance.now() clock at host-timer resolution", reducing the native command's rationale to merely "running the analyze ... with a native monotonic clock". This matters beyond wording: this file documents why a SECOND native query surface was granted an exception past the removed pre-wired commands. Weakening a security/scope rationale with an untrue premise degrades the record a future reviewer relies on to judge whether the exception is still warranted. The doc-comment on the test at line ~104 is likewise softened from "the datum the wasm path fundamentally cannot provide" to a neutral statement, removing the contrast that actually motivates the test.
issues.fix_hint: Restore the original justification. The native command's raison d'être — being the only source that can measure per-operator wall time, because wasm32 has no usable monotonic clock — remains factually correct at this head and should not be diluted.
issues.title: Rewrites the documented justification for the reviewed native-query exception on a false premise

issues.body: The [data-plan-analyze] button title becomes "...trace per-operator rows, q-error, and wall time at browser timer resolution", and the module header changes the IN-TAB bullet from "wall times unmeasured on wasm32" to "structured ANALYZE wall times use performance.now() at browser host-timer resolution". Both advertise a measurement the code does not perform (crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs:4846). The tooltip is the primary affordance a user reads before choosing in-tab ANALYZE over the native path, so the overclaim actively steers users away from the only source that gives them what the tooltip promises.
issues.fix_hint: Revert both strings to the unmeasured wording so the tooltip matches what the in-tab run actually produces.
issues.title: ANALYZE button tooltip and module header assert unbacked wall-time measurement

issues.body: The explain_native registration comment now states "Structured in-tab wasm ANALYZE also measures wall time, through performance.now() at browser timer resolution." This directly contradicts crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs:4845-4847 (`Instant` is unusable on wasm32-unknown-unknown ... `let nanos = 0u64;`) and crates/sparq-wasm/src/explain_plan.rs:26,56, which remain unmodified by this PR and are still correct. The repo now carries two mutually exclusive statements about the same value, with the false one sitting next to the security note about the strict-empty egress allowlist.
issues.fix_hint: Revert to the accurate statement that the in-tab wasm engine reads 0 nanos and only the native engine measures real per-operator wall time.
issues.title: Command-registration comment contradicts the engine's own wasm32 timing code

issues.body: formatNanos and hotOperatorPath docs are rewritten so 0 means "sub-resolution or unmeasured" and hotOperatorPath returns null for "work below the host timer's resolution" instead of "a wasm ANALYZE where every node reads 0". The formatting behaviour is unchanged and still correct, but the documented SEMANTICS of '—' now imply a measurement was attempted and rounded to zero. At this head every wasm value is a hard-coded constant, never a measurement. This is the library-level source of the false story the UI strings repeat, so leaving it in place would keep re-seeding the overclaim into future docs even if the visible strings were fixed.
issues.fix_hint: Restore the 'wasm ANALYZE reads 0 = unmeasured (no monotonic clock on wasm32)' framing. If a real browser clock is added later, 'sub-resolution' becomes accurate and can be introduced together with that code.
issues.title: Reframes 0 nanos from 'unmeasured' to 'sub-resolution', silently changing what the UI's '—' means

issues.body: The header and the two inline comments are changed so `formatNanos(0) === '—'` is justified by "0 is sub-resolution/unmeasured" and the hotOperatorPath zeros case by "a host timer can report 0 for work below its resolution", replacing the accurate "wasm32 reads 0 = unmeasured". The assertions themselves are unchanged and still valid, so this is not a broken test — but the comments are the only place these cases record WHY they exist, and rewriting them onto a false premise removes the traceability that would let a future maintainer spot the drift. The test name change ('no measured time (dry run / wasm zeros)' to 'no positive time (dry run / sub-resolution zeros)') has the same effect.
issues.fix_hint: Revert the comments and the test name; the assertions are correct as-is and need no change.
issues.title: Test comments rewritten to describe the zeros as measured sub-resolution values, removing the honesty rationale the assertions encode

issues.body: The doc-comment drops "the datum the in-tab wasm engine fundamentally cannot provide (reads 0, no monotonic clock)" and substitutes "Structured in-tab wasm ANALYZE measures them through performance.now() at browser timer resolution." Same false premise as the other surfaces; lower severity only because this is an internal API doc rather than user-visible text.
issues.fix_hint: Revert alongside the other doc reverts so the IPC layer's description matches crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs:4846.
issues.title: nativeServiceQuery/explain_native doc repeats the unbacked wasm-timing claim

issues.body: Taking the PR's intent charitably as a doc reconciliation, it is still incomplete: it rewrites only the GUI/tauri layer while the engine and wasm-binding layers retain the opposite (correct) statement — crates/sparq-engine/src/explain_json.rs:32 ('On wasm32 the wall nanos are always 0'), :66-67, :346, :361, and crates/sparq-wasm/src/explain_plan.rs:26,56 — and the live wasm32 test crates/sparq-wasm/tests/web.rs:949-956 asserts `"nanos":0` in its name and body. A reconciliation that leaves the source of truth stating the opposite of the presentation layer produces exactly the doc drift the repo's honesty rules exist to prevent.
issues.fix_hint: Whichever direction is chosen, make it complete and consistent across engine, wasm binding, its wasm32 test, and the GUI. Given the code as written, the consistent direction is to revert the GUI prose to match the engine.
issues.title: Change is internally inconsistent with undiffed authoritative docs and the live wasm test — incomplete even on its own terms

verdict.summary: This is a documentation/string-only PR (no implementation change anywhere in the diff) that rewrites an ACCURATE honesty disclosure into a FALSE measurement claim. It asserts that structured in-tab wasm ANALYZE now measures per-operator wall time through the browser's performance.now() clock. That is not true at the PR head. The engine hard-codes the value: crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs:4846-4847 has `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")] let nanos = 0u64;` with the comment `Instant is unusable on wasm32-unknown-unknown (it panics): rows only there`. Nothing on the path injects a browser clock: crates/sparq-wasm/src/explain_plan.rs:62 calls sparq_engine::explain_plan_analyze and returns PlanNode::to_json() verbatim, and the GUI (gui/app/src/lib/engine-context.tsx:1338) passes that JSON straight into parsePlanJson, which is a bare JSON.parse (packages/sparq-client/src/plan.ts:92-94). A repo-wide grep for `performance.now` across crates/ and gui/ returns zero call sites. The live wasm32 test crates/sparq-wasm/tests/web.rs:949-956 (`explain_plan_analyze_json_fills_actuals_zero_nanos`) still asserts `"nanos":0`, and the authoritative module docs (crates/sparq-engine/src/explain_json.rs:32,66-67,346,361; crates/sparq-wasm/src/explain_plan.rs:26,56) still correctly document 0/no-monotonic-clock. So every wasm operator reports 0 nanos and renders as an em dash, while the new user-facing text tells the user those times WERE measured and merely fell below timer resolution. That inverts the meaning of the display for every wasm ANALYZE. The e2e change makes this worse: the spec now asserts the note contains "performance.now() clock", pinning the false statement as the expected behaviour (a wrong-oracle test that passes precisely because the string is hard-coded). The change also rewrites the documented justification for the reviewed native-query exception in gui/src-tauri.
